title: Photosynthesis
standard_text: Cell requirements and energy; ATP; the light-dependent reactions and the Calvin cycle; factors that affect the rate of photosynthesis. (summary of the Strengthened Senior High School curriculum, Biology 1, Quarter 2)
meta_desc: Free Biology 1 worksheets (Strengthened SHS curriculum, Quarter 2): photosynthesis, photosynthesis in leaves, early experiments and pigments, the light phase and the dark phase and limiting factors. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: The oxygen released comes from water.
body_html:
How to think about it

Photosynthesis takes place in the chloroplasts. In the light-dependent reactions (in the thylakoids), light energy splits water, releases oxygen and makes ATP and NADPH. In the Calvin cycle (in the stroma), ATP and NADPH are used to fix carbon dioxide into sugar.

The rate of photosynthesis is limited by whichever factor is in shortest supply: light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration or temperature. Farmers and greenhouse growers control these factors to increase crop yields.

Example

Which gas is released in photosynthesis?

It comes from water.

Answer: oxygen

Example

Light is increased but the rate stays the same. Why?

Another factor is limiting.

Answer: CO₂ or temperature is now limiting

Common mistakes

  • Thinking plants get their food from the soil.
  • Thinking the oxygen comes from CO₂.
  • Thinking the dark phase only happens at night.

faq.q: Why are leaves destarched before a starch test?
faq.a: So that any starch found must have been made during the experiment.

faq.q: Why is photosynthesis important for all life?
faq.a: It produces food (glucose) and oxygen and removes carbon dioxide from the air.

items.q: Why does the rate of an enzyme reaction rise between 10 °C and 35 °C?
c: molecules have more kinetic energy, so enzyme–substrate collisions are more frequent
items.e: Above the optimum, denaturation takes over.

items.q: What is a limiting factor?
c: the factor that is present in excess
the temperature at which an enzyme denatures
a factor that stops a reaction for ever
the factor that is in shortest supply and so controls the rate
items.e: Light, CO₂ and temperature limit photosynthesis.

items.q: What is made in anaerobic respiration in human muscle?
items.e: Yeast makes ethanol and CO₂ instead.

items.q: Why is anaerobic respiration much less efficient than aerobic respiration?
c: glucose is only partly broken down, so much less ATP is made
it makes no ATP at all
items.e: Energy is left in lactate or ethanol.

items.q: What is RuBP?
c: a 5-carbon compound that combines with CO₂ in the Calvin cycle
items.e: Ribulose bisphosphate is regenerated using ATP.

items.q: A water plant gives off 36 bubbles of oxygen in 4 minutes. What is the rate of photosynthesis in bubbles per minute?
